## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Lotte Zweig an Hannah Altmann [4. August 1940], SZ-AAL/B1.40
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.40
- Datum: 4.8.1940
- Objekttyp: Brief

pages.transcription:
Wyndham Hotel				4.August 1940.

Dear Hanna,
I was so glad to get the first letter from you this
morning and to hear what is going on in "Rosemount" and in the
family. What a shame that Levintals did not come and apparently
let you down in not too nice a way! I hope that at least Orchard
found for you some nice people, for it is a terrible thought that
you should have to remain in Bath while the children are in London
only because there is no one else to look after it. I am glad that
you had Lizzie with you who is such a good friend to you, and I wish
I could be with you again. But we have to start travelling again on
Friday and have still a very busy time these last few days. Besides
packing and all the necessary formalities Stefan has started - at
first just for fun - to work on a film subject with a friend and now
they are working and dictating to me, and it takes most of our time
just now. Within the next few days I shall definitely decide where
Eva will stay - Rose is to bring me together with a family who are
very eager to take a child - and I shall then cable you the name
and address of Eva's future home and it will be best if you commu-
nicate directly with them. As I wrote you yesterday, my sister-in-
law offered to fetch her from the boat, and so will Rose if she is
back from her holiday - but I think it best if she goes directly
with the people where she will stay. But it is good to know that my
sister-in-law as well as Rose will later on visit her and see whether
she is well looked after and happy. My sister-in-law/s address is
Rose Wohl Stefanie Zweig, 18 West 70th Street, New York, and Roses 25 East
77th Street, New York, and I shall keep both exactly informed about
everything so that you can communicate with either of them if you
want to. - As to Eva's clothes, there is nothing specially American
you have to get for her. Just bear in mind that the summers are very
hot here, the winters very cold and that the houses are rather over-
heated than otherwise. Schools don't have uniforms. - As to bringing
Ursula over, I have little hope. The English reentry permit which
the Committee wrongly asked for Eva will, I am afraid, will be
essential for getting a visitor's visa for Ursula. And from what I
have heard so far from similar cases it is as good as impossible.
But I shall enquire again and let you know. -
We are sailing with the "Argentina"(American Republics
Line) on the 9th and should arrive in Rio on the 21st. If necessary
you could also cable us to the boat during the crossing. How long
we will stay there and where we go from then is not yet certain. Lat
on we hope to get permission to come back here, perhaps for a lect
tour. -
You did not say a word about Mama in your letter. I
suppose that means she is allright and still with Mathiasson.
We are happy to know that Orchard and Ingram are helpful and zeal friends
and that you also have good friends in London. Do you know by
chance whether Isaacs has taken over Korner's flat in Bath and
did you meet them? I liked them very much and I suppose you
would feel the same. Did you hear from Korner in the meantime?
Hoping that Eva will soon arrive safely and
that you are all keeping well,

7 sent this letter by clipper also				Lotte
pages.notes: Typoskript mit handschriftlichen Ergänzungen am linken Rand ('Rose Wohl') und am Ende ('7 sent this letter by clipper also').

I should not be economical in
